title: 📞 The Duplex story: ten years of automated calls until it runs on Gemini 4!
body: 📞 The Duplex story: ten years of automated calls until it runs on Gemini 4!

Google revealed in a new technical post the story of Duplex, the technology that calls shops on your behalf, and how it evolved over ten years from a narrow, closed system to general AI running on Gemini 4 models.

In the beginning, before the era of modern language models, the system worked with models customised for each task separately: one model for restaurant bookings and another for asking about opening hours, and engineers had to teach it every possible scenario in the call.

In 2022 the system began using generative models in live calls, then came the big shift, when the restrictions were lifted entirely: it became enough to describe the task in free words, and the system understands what is required and adapts to any new situation — such as requesting a seat near the window or space for a baby stroller — without building a new model for each case.

Today Duplex works inside the "Tasks" feature in the Gemini app, with the Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon models: it calls shops when there is no online booking, analyses service bills, executes payments securely, and coordinates with you via email and messages.

Every call begins by clarifying that it comes from a Google automated system, and any shop can stop these calls from its business profile settings, or by saying "stop calling my shop" during the call, without installing any software.

One striking figure: information about shops that Duplex gathered from its calls appeared in Search and Maps more than a trillion times — meaning a single call may answer the questions of thousands of users later.

Simply put: a technology that began ten years ago as a system memorising ready-made scenarios is today an AI that understands any request and calls and negotiates on your behalf. Would you trust an assistant that calls shops and speaks in your name?
Would you let an AI assistant call shops on your behalf?
